standard_prerequisites: Same chapter: lemma-degree-minimal-polynomial (deg of the minimal polynomial equals the subextension degree) and lemma-multiplicativity-degrees (delivered card L48338) for e deg(P) = [L : K]; Cayley-Hamilton; minimal polynomial divides the characteristic polynomial
core_obligations: Choose a basis beta_1, ..., beta_e of L over K(alpha); then L is the direct sum of the alpha-invariant subspaces K(alpha) beta_i, so the characteristic polynomial of alpha on L is the e-th power of the characteristic polynomial of alpha on K(alpha)
For L = K(alpha): Cayley-Hamilton makes alpha a root of the characteristic polynomial, so the minimal polynomial divides it, and the two have the same degree, whence they are equal
Combining: the characteristic polynomial of alpha : L -> L equals P^e with e deg(P) = [L : K]
proof_roadmap: Split L into alpha-invariant summands and exponentiate
Settle the simple case by Cayley-Hamilton and the degree count
